stem: In the above-mentioned systematic review, which of the following is the best way to proceed for combining the data from individual studies?
options: Meta-analysis is not possible as the individual trials are not RCTs
Combine all data in a single meta-analysis using a random effects model
Combine all data and carry out a fixed effects analysis
Deal with two sets of data differently and carry out two independent meta-analysis
Meta-analysis must be abandoned as methods differ
correctAnswer: Deal with two sets of data differently and carry out two independent meta-analysis
explanation: Meta-analysis is a best done using studies with a common methodology (all RCTs, all case-control studies) etc., But increasingly certain meta- analytical papers seem to override this tradition. Dealing with methodologically different data separately and reporting the results independently is the best way forward for the above example. 

stem: In which of the following situations a random effects analysis is indicated in a meta-analysis?
options: Presence of too few studies for efficient combining
Meta-analysis of studies other than RCTs.
explanation: When combining the outcomes from different studies, one may use a fixed and/or random effects model. A fixed effects model assumes that all the studies share the same common treatment effect while a random effects model assumes that they do not share the same common treatment effect. In fixed effect analysis the inference is restricted to included set of studies. It assumes that only random error within studies could explain observed differences. It ignores between-study variations (hence heterogeneity). So this can be applied only if  heterogeneity can be safely excluded by testing for it. Random effects analysis assumes that each study shows a different effect which are normally distributed around true mean. This assumption gives proportionally greater weight to smaller studies. Hence this model is susceptible to publication bias and results in wider less precise confidence intervals.

stem: A reviewer notes the following while undertaking a literature search to identify the effect of vitamin E on tardive dyskinesia. Many small studies are published only when they show a positive result in favour of vitamin E. But larger studies are published with both directions of results. If the reviewer constructs an inverted funnel plot which of the following will be seen?
options: The plot will be asymmetrical due to the absence of small negative studies.
The plot cannot be constructed due to the lack of negative small studies
The plot will be smaller in size due to the presence of small studies
The plot will be asymmetrical due to the presence of large studies in both directions of results
correctAnswer: The plot will be asymmetrical due to the absence of small negative studies.
explanation: The most common method to detect publication bias is to investigate the presence of asymmetry in (inverted) funnel plots. A funnel plot shows the relation between study effect size and its precision. Small studies are more likely to remain unpublished if their results are  nonsignificant or unfavourable, and larger studies get published regardless. This leads to funnel-plot asymmetry. Although visual inspection of funnel plots is unreliable, statistical tests can be used to quantify the asymmetry.

stem: Which of the following best describes effect size measured in meta-analyses?
options: Difference in outcome between intervention and control groups
Ratio of outcome between intervention and control groups divided by standard deviation
Difference in outcome between intervention and control groups in terms of standard deviation of the outcome in the population
Odds of having an outcome due to intervention
Ratio of outcome between intervention and control groups
correctAnswer: Difference in outcome between intervention and control groups in terms of standard deviation of the outcome in the population
explanation: Effect size is the difference in mean scores between the treatment and control groups divided by the standard deviation of the scores in the control group (or the pooled standard deviation of the treatment and control groups, or the pooled standard deviation of the change score). As you might have noted, this does not have units that vary with outcome scales; hence it is possible to pool data from various studies in a meta-analysis using effect-size. Guyatt G Rennie D et al. Users' guide to the medical literature: JAMA evidence 2nd ed. McGrawHill 2008. Pg  736

stem: Which one of the following could be classified as grey literature for the purpose of a systematic review?
options: Peer reviewed articles indexed in PsycINFO
Theses work recently submitted to universities
correctAnswer: Theses work recently submitted to universities
explanation: Searching for grey literature is often difficult as there is no single source of grey literature, and the sources are usually websites that are not indexed and can be difficult to search. Such grey literature includes theses, unpublished abstracts at conferences, monographs and proceedings from conventions, etc. 

stem: In a weekly journal club, your clinical tutor points out significant publication bias in the studies selected for a systematic review. He constructs a funnel plot to support his arguments. What is the most likely explanation for publication bias
options: Editors accept only those articles that are written by experts
Systematic reviewers discard weaker studies in meta-analysis
Researchers withhold negative results from publication
Authors submit studies with low sample size to non-indexed journals
Editors accept only those articles with which they agree
correctAnswer: Researchers withhold negative results from publication
explanation: Publication bias has been defined as "the tendency on the part of investigators to submit, or the reviewers and editors, to accept manuscripts based on the direction or strength of the study findings". As a result, the strongest and most positive studies are most likely to be published. "Perhaps the common misconception is that most work remains unpublished because of rejection from chosen journals.  However, investigators have found the contrary to be true. Rejection of manuscripts by journals has been found to be less important than failure of researchers to actually submit their work for publication.Failure to submit manuscripts can be caused by a number of factors including unimportant results, incomplete analysis, and investigators being too busy or having lost interest. This lack of enthusiasm to publish has been coined the 'file drawer problem-. Dickersin K, Min Y, Meinert C. Factors influencing publication of research results. JAMA 1992; 267: 374-378 (Publication bias: raising awareness of a potential problem. Excerpts retrieved from http://www.nature.com/bdj/journal/v194/n5/full/4809923a.html).

stem: Meta-analyses that summarise data from multiple studies are needed because
options: Individual studies are susceptible to confounding
Individual studies often use higher threshold of p values
Individual studies often lack sufficient power for generalised conclusions
Individual studies are prone to measurement errors
correctAnswer: Individual studies often lack sufficient power for generalised conclusions
explanation: Remember GIGO principle in secondary research: Garbage in - Garbage out! The quality of a systematic review or meta-analysis depends on the quality of individual studies. Hence error or bias-prone individual studies cannot be replaced by a meta-analyses of those studies. But pooled data in a secondary study such as meta-analysis has larger sample size to achieve better precision. 

stem: In a study examining the relationship between domestic abuse and depression, women who do and do not suffer abuse are followed up over a five-year period. explanation: This is a follow-up in a prospective manner where exposure is determined at the outset. This is a cohort study.

stem: A cross-sectional comparison of the incidence of schizophrenia at three periods 1881-1902, 1978-1980 and 1992-1994 was performed using hospital admission records at Mapperley Hospital, Nottingham. Research diagnostic criteria were applied retrospectively to determine the diagnosis. It was concluded that no significant changes in the incidence of schizophrenia occurred across the 114 years considered in the study. Which of the following, if present, can invalidate such a conclusion?
explanation: Any study comparing incidence rates must have a specified denominator; in this case it will be mid-period population during the observed  years. This study is a retrospective survey - we do not need randomisation or interventions to answer the research question.

stem: National Comorbidity Survey examined a possible association between traits of neuroticism and lifetime prevalence of various psychiatric disorders. Trained non-clinical staff screened randomly chosen individuals using well-validated questionnaires to establish lifetime diagnoses in addition to collecting data on drug use, alcohol intake and various personality traits. What type of study is this?
explanation: Most epidemiological studies are cross-sectional surveys where point prevalence and/or lifetime prevalence are estimated. 

stem: Which of the following correctly describes ecological fallacy
options: Erroneous result due to selecting smaller groups instead of larger groups
Erroneous result due to selecting larger groups instead of smaller groups
Ascribing the characteristics of a group to all individuals in that group
Failure to examine temporal relationships between exposures and outcomes
Failure to examine dose response relationship while claiming causal asociation
correctAnswer: Ascribing the characteristics of a group to all individuals in that group
explanation: An ecological fallacy is "an error in the interpretation of statistical data in an ecological study, whereby inferences about the nature of specific individuals are based solely upon aggregate statistics collected for the group to which those individuals belong" (http://wiki.gis.com/wiki/index.php/Ecological_fallacy). 

stem: Retrospective cohort studies are characterized by all of the following except
options: The required sample size is smaller than that needed for a prospective cohort study
They are useful for rare exposures
The study groups are exposed and nonexposed
The required sample size is similar to that needed for a prospective cohort study
correctAnswer: The required sample size is smaller than that needed for a prospective cohort study 
explanation: The only difference from prospective study is in calendar timings of data collection and, as a result, the requirement for case registers/records to tease out data when doing a retrospective cohort study

stem: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of a prospective cohort study?
options: Recall bias is minimized compared with a case-control study
Precise measurement of exposure is possible
It usually costs less than a case-control study
Many disease outcomes can be studied simultaneously
correctAnswer: It usually costs less than a case-control study 
explanation: Time resources, manpower and monetary costs are higher though cohort studies may offer more value for research investment when compared to multiple case-control studies

stem: Which one of the following is a disadvantage of carrying out a cohort study?
options: For a disease with high incidence, large amount of subjects will be needed to complete the study
Dose response effect cannot be identified
explanation: Cohort studies are usually prospective; they are costly and time consuming, and some can span for many decades. The ability to ascertain the temporal correlation between exposure and an outcome is a major strength of cohort design. For diseases that occur at a high frequency on exposure, a relatively smaller cohort should be sufficient when compared to rare diseases. 

stem: Which of the following study design is best suited to evaluate properties of a screening tool?
explanation: It is important to administer both gold standard and the evaluated tool to all study subjects. A cross sectional design is often used for this purpose.
